title: Chicken, NS as to part, rotisserie

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide. The “rotisserie” form refers to cooking a whole bird on a rotating spit, which helps retain juiciness and flavor. The skin may be eaten or removed according to personal preference.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken provides all essential amino acids required by humans.
Rotisserie cooking distributes heat evenly, resulting in tender meat.
Chicken skin is rich in collagen, beneficial for skin and joint health.
There are countless cultural recipes for rotisserie chicken, from Mediterranean to Asian styles.
Free‑range chickens often have superior taste and texture.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken meat supplies complete protein that supports muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low fat (skin‑less)
items.content: Removing the skin dramatically reduces calories and saturated fat content.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken is a good source of niacin, vitamin B6, and B12, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It contains phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bone health and immunity.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: The high protein level helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Raw chicken may harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter, so it must be cooked to an internal temperature of 165 °F (75 °C).

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to chicken proteins.

items.title: High sodium in processed products
items.content: Marinated or smoked chicken products often contain added salt.

items.title: Skin fat
items.content: Eating the skin adds saturated fat and extra calories.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rotisserie chicken can be served whole, sliced into portions, added to salads, sandwiches, or rice dishes. The skin can be left for a crispy crust or removed to reduce fat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked chicken in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags for 2‑3 months. Thaw in the fridge, not at room temperature.
